title: Recordanelles capture transient gene expression in single human cells - Nature Biotechnology
gist: Nature Biotechnology research summary: a synthetic organelle called the recordanelle can record cellular RNAs in human cells for several days and be read out with single-cell sensitivity, overcoming the snapshot limit of RNA sequencing. The page is paywalled preview text with a short reference list contrasting it with CRISPR, prime-editing, virus-like-particle and vault-particle recorders.

insights.claim: Standard RNA sequencing gives high-resolution snapshots of a cell's transcriptome but cannot capture transient changes in individual cells over long periods at transcriptome-wide scale.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: The gap in time-resolved single-cell transcriptomics is the market need that recording tools target.
insights.quote: RNA sequencing can capture high-resolution snapshots of a cell’s transcriptome, but transient changes in individual cells cannot be captured over long periods at a transcriptome-wide scale.
insights.locator: RNA sequencing can capture high-resolution snapshots

insights.claim: The recordanelle, a synthetic organelle, can record cellular RNAs in human cells for several days and be read with single-cell sensitivity.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: A new synthetic-biology tool for archiving transient gene expression; watch for follow-on adoption and licensing.
insights.quote: a synthetic organelle termed the ‘recordanelle’ can record cellular RNAs in cells for several days and be read with single-cell sensitivity
insights.locator: RNA sequencing can capture high-resolution snapshots

insights.claim: Prior recording approaches cited include CRISPR spacer acquisition from RNA in prokaryotic cells and prime-editing-based DNA typewriting, so the recordanelle targets human cells with a different, organelle-based mechanism.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Molecular recording is a crowded academic field with several competing modalities.

insights.claim: Two 2026 papers describe alternative transcriptome recorders: engineered virus-like particles that export RNAs into the medium (Cell), and a vault-particle-based RNA storage device (Science).
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Several groups are converging on non-destructive transcriptome recording in the same year, signalling a hot area.

insights.claim: The summary is a commentary on Reinkemeier et al. in Nature Biotechnology, published 22 October 2026, and is subject-tagged molecular biology and synthetic biology; full text sits behind a subscription (USD 39.95 per article).
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Full-paper details are in the companion article, so this page carries little evidence by itself.
